prompt: Fix firstIndex(a, x) for a sorted ascending integer array. Return the first matching zero-based index, or -1 if absent. Preserve logarithmic worst-case search.
starter: module.exports = function firstIndex(a,x){ let l=0,r=a.length-1; while(l<=r){const m=(l+r)>>>1; if(a[m]===x)return m; if(a[m]<x)l=m+1;else r=m-1;}return -1;};

prompt: Fix mergeRanges(ranges). Return sorted merged inclusive integer ranges, merging overlaps and adjacent intervals. Do not mutate the input or its pairs; range endpoints are ordered and safely within +/- 1 billion.

Implement simulate(capacity, ops), returning an array of outputs for get operations only. Ops are ['put',key,value] or ['get',key]. Missing keys return null; a successful get or any put makes that entry most recently used. Evict the least recently used on overflow. Capacity zero stores nothing. Keys are strings; values are integers.

Implement parseRow(row): parse a single CSV record into strings, preserving empty fields and spaces. Only fields starting with a double quote can be quoted; doubled quotes inside a quoted field mean a literal quote. Return null for malformed quoting or trailing characters after the closing quote before comma/end. No unquoted CR or LF. An empty row is one empty field.

Implement buildOrder(nodes, deps). nodes is a unique array of ASCII names; deps is an array of [prerequisite, dependent] pairs, all names known. Return the lexicographically smallest valid topological order, or null on cycles. Ignore duplicate edges.

Replace the floating-point parser price(s). Accept only ASCII decimal strings matching an optional leading '-' then one or more digits, and optionally a dot with one or two digits. Return the exact amount in cents as a canonical decimal string with no leading zeros (negative zero is '0'). Input can exceed Number precision. Return null on malformed input.

Refactor summarize(rows) to include every string label safely, including JavaScript object prototype names. Return an array of [label,count,total] triples in order of first appearance. Each row is [label, integer duration]. Do not mutate input.

Implement splitWords(s) for a small command-line text format; only tokenize, never execute. Unquoted ASCII spaces and tabs separate words. Single and double quotes group text and concatenate with adjacent text; empty quoted text creates a word. Backslash escapes the next character outside single quotes, including inside double quotes. Return null for an unclosed quote or trailing unescaped backslash.
